steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Scrub potato and dry well; prick all over with a fork. Season skin with salt.
Bake directly on the center rack of the preheated oven until easily pierced with a fork, about 1 1/2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Potato
raw_recipe.description: Try this simple baked potato recipe for a spud with crunchy skin and soft, tender flesh, guaranteed every time.

review.reviewBody:
Recipe is great if you have a lot of time to spare. My mother taught me to make potatoes fast and they come out just the same. 
1.Poke a bunch of holes on each potatoe with a fork (to make sure they dont explode)
2. Put in microwave for 10 minutes (3-8 potatoes) (7 minutes for 1-2 potatoes)
3. With an oven mit take the potatoes out of the microwave and wrap in tinfoil individually and place in a preheated oven at 375.
4. Bake 20 minutes or until soft and squishey. (You can check the potatoes with an oven mit on to see if they are cooked and squishey enough to eat.
5. Garnish with what ever you like!

Four stars that should be 4.5. There are as many recipes for baked potatoes as there are people. This is a very good recipe, but not as good as the recipe from England (Britain) where jacketed (baked) potatoes are a staple in every restaurant, pub, street vendor and home. I found a number of recipes there and tried them here in the US. I found that our russet potatoes are a bit different than those in England, Ireland, and Scotland. Our soil is different, for one thing, so there will be flavor differences. Also, the butter is superior to ours because of higher fat content. 

Personally, I follow an English recipe for "English Jacket Potatoes" that I found on Pinterest. It requires a baking time of approximately 2 hours so it is time consuming. Unlike the English recipe, I also roll them in coarse sea salt before baking and put them right on the top oven rack. I use Kerrygold unsalted butter and a lot of it, just as it is served there. A little Maldon salt after opening them finishes my meal. The skins are very crisp and need extra butter, but are sensational.

I've tried making baked potatoes before but never knew the secret of how to make the skin crispy until I found this recipe.I start with huge Russet potatoes,add oil and sea salt, microwave them for 10 minutes then bake them at 400 degrees for one hour and they turn out perfect.Add sour cream, bacon, green onions, salt and pepper, and shredded cheddar and you've got a meal.

Excellent recipe.

A little mod:
Key are:
Low heat (325) slow cooking.
I use olive oil over the skin (low boiling point and very tasty oil).
Cook 90 minutes, while cooking mix sour cream, bacon bits (real bacon please!), salt/pepper and chopped chive together.
Let that sit.
pull potato out, cut the top of it and gently scoop the meat out of potato, mix meat with your sour cream and back in the potato nice and tight, add cheddar cheese and back in the oven 10 minutes with the 'lid' on the side.
Pull out put the lid on and serve!!!

I cant eat regular potatoes, Diabetic, so I used a sweetpotato .did it in the Microwave cooked very well, also dont use sale I use salt free Onion & Garlick power, also added Tumerick & a dash of Spicy Paperika, was great.

I followed one review of poking holes in them and microwaving for 15 minutes. Then I brush with olive oil and sea salt and bake them at 375 for about 20 minutes and they are perfect!! I use Yukon gold potatoes...they are the best!

okay people..... try 400 for one hour. pour some kosher salt onto the counter. put some butter in your hands and fondle your potato. then pat the salt with your buttery palm and tap onto sticky potato. wash your hands and set right onto oven rack with tongs and cook for 1 hour. your skin will be crispy and there is absolutely no reason to wait 1.5 hours for a potato, unless you are cooking something else at 350 for an hour and a half. good luck!

Very simple, but much tastier than a microwave potato.

I followed the recommendation to put olive oil, and salt on the outside. I think this added a whole new flavor to the potato, and will do this from now on.

My medium russets were done in about 70 mins @ 325.
Mmm! Tastes so good with melted cheese and bacon bits! I would DEFINITELY recommend it! It's simple, easy, and takes no time at all if you're using a microwave instead!

Excellent, simple recipe; like some, I'll coat with Pam olive or similar, or even rub with olive oil, then sprinkle or roll in various seasonings depending on my mood that night. Finishing it on the grill after baking gives it a smokey taste that makes this recipe hard to beat. Thanks!

This is a very good basic recipe. I wrap mine in foil. Rub a little butter or margarine on the potato. Cut it in half and put a big slice of sweet onion in the middle and wrap up in foil. Even if you don't like onion you can discard and just eat the potato. We love oninons. It give the potato a great flavor. I perfer yukon gold. But It would work with other potatoes.
After pricking my potatoes with a fork and placing them directly on the oven rack, my oven began to smoke from the drippings. Not sure how to prevent this yet still get crispy skins.
One of the best garden staples, a baked potato flourishes when accompanied by fibrous green onions, diced tomato, and black olives. Add whatever you need for flavor -- mmmmMm good!

I just needed the cooking time and this was perfect. To everyone who keeps complaining about time and recommends microwaving, it is not the same. A BAKED potato tastes soooo much better than a microwaved spud.
Thanks for the easy instructions on making a baked potato! I had forgotten how, and this is so helpful.
I added my own topping. The baked potatoes came out crispy on the outside and soft and tender on the inside. Delicious!

I only want to comment. I rated 5 because I think it's a great idea to have these kinds of simple instructions for the beginner and then have the seasoned cooks add their techniques. I've been making baked potatoes for years but never thought to add seasonings to the potato skin before baking! I love that idea! Thankss

These potatoes were amazing!!! My whole family ate them all. Next time I have to make more for dinner. We stuffed them full of butter, sour cream, green onions, and cheese and ate them like tacos. So fattening and generally not the way I feed my family, but it was a wonderful treat!!
I actually made my baked potatoes the way Heather R did, and they turned out perfectly! Thanks :)

Potatoes are pretty good. What I did differently was that I used canola oil instead of vegetable oil (because I didn't have vegetable oil) and instead of salt I used seasoned salt. The one thing that I hate about the recipe is the 1 1/2 our wait.
